source_evidence: Each firm’s relationship summary uses similar headings and order of topics to make it easy for you to compare firms.
answer: A client relationship summary, also called Form CRS, is a document that helps retail investors understand and compare a firm’s services. It describes the services offered, fees and costs, conflicts of interest, standards of conduct, and any reportable legal or disciplinary history. For comparing brokers and investment advisers, it can help clarify differences in service: brokers’ services are generally more transactional and time-specific, while advisers’ services are generally more focused on a portfolio or account over time. The summary also includes questions to ask a financial professional.
